questions.question_text: Learning:

options.text: Is a temporary change in observable behaviour
Does not require prior experience
Includes behavioural changes caused by maturation
Includes behavioural changes due to drug effects
Does not include behavioural changes due to hunger

correct_answer.text: Does not include behavioural changes due to hunger

correct_answers.text: Does not include behavioural changes due to hunger

questions.explanation: Learning is a relatively permanent change, from prior experience, and does not include changes through maturation and temporary conditions like drug effects, hunger, fatigue, etc.

questions.question_text: In Pavlov's experiments:

options.text: Salivation was an unconditioned stimulus before conditioning
Salivation was a conditioned stimulus after conditioning
Food was a conditioned stimulus after conditioning
Light was a conditioned stimulus after conditioning
None of the above is correct

correct_answer.text: Light was a conditioned stimulus after conditioning

correct_answers.text: Light was a conditioned stimulus after conditioning

questions.explanation: Salivation was an unconditioned response before the conditioning, and a conditioned response after conditioning. Food was an unconditioned stimulus.

questions.question_text: Regarding classical conditioning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The conditioned response is an acquired response to a conditioned stimulus
The acquisition stage is the period in which an association is acquired between conditioned stimulus and conditioned response
In delayed conditioning the onset of the conditioned stimulus precedes that of an unconditioned stimulus
In delayed conditioning the conditioned stimulus continues until the response occurs
Delayed conditioning is optimal when the delay between the onset of the two stimuli is around half a second

correct_answer.text: The acquisition stage is the period in which an association is acquired between conditioned stimulus and conditioned response

correct_answers.text: The acquisition stage is the period in which an association is acquired between conditioned stimulus and conditioned response

questions.explanation: The acquisition stage is the period in which an association is acquired between conditioned stimulus and unconditioned stimulus.

questions.question_text: In classical conditioning:

options.text: The subject is active in learning
Response is typically autonomic or emotional
Spontaneous recovery is stronger than a conditioned response
The longer the time between extinction and reappearance, the weaker is the response
The strength of the conditioned response is inversely proportional to the intensity of the stimulus

correct_answer.text: Response is typically autonomic or emotional

correct_answers.text: Response is typically autonomic or emotional

questions.explanation: The subject is passive; spontaneous recovery is weaker than conditioned response; the longer the time between extinction and reappearance, the stronger is the response; the strength of the conditioned response is directly proportional to the intensity of the stimulus.

questions.question_text: Regarding classical conditioning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Forward conditioning: conditioned stimulus (CS) comes first, and while it is still happening the unconditioned stimulus (UCS) occurs
Simultaneous conditioning: CS and UCS occur at the same time
Trace conditioning: CS comes first, and after it stops UCS occurs
Backward conditioning: CS occurs after UCS has started
Delayed conditioning: CS occurs after UCS has started and stops before UCS stops

correct_answer.text: Delayed conditioning: CS occurs after UCS has started and stops before UCS stops

correct_answers.text: Delayed conditioning: CS occurs after UCS has started and stops before UCS stops

questions.explanation: Delayed conditioning is the same as forward conditioning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of extinction?

options.text: It occurs in both classical and operant conditioning
It is the same as forgetting
Usually the complete loss of the conditioned stimulus occurs
Merely not presenting the conditioned stimulus will result in the extinction of the conditioned response after some time.
Relearning of extinguished associations is usually slower than learning in controls

correct_answer.text: It occurs in both classical and operant conditioning

correct_answers.text: It occurs in both classical and operant conditioning

questions.explanation: Extinction is not the same as forgetting; partial recovery occurs; it needs repeat presentation of a conditioned stimulus without an unconditioned stimulus; relearning is quicker.

questions.question_text: Regarding generalization:

options.text: It accounts in part for an individual's ability to react to novel stimuli that are similar to familiar ones
It occurs frequently in everyday life
The response will vary in strength as a function of similarity
It is a stimulus similar to the original stimulus eliciting the conditioned response
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Generalization is a process whereby once a conditioned response has been established to a given stimulus, that response is evoked by a similar stimulus. The strength of response is inversely proportional to the difference between two stimuli.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of discrimination in classical conditioning?

options.text: It is a reaction to differences
When distinguishing similar but different stimuli one is reinforced and the other is not
It is brought about through differential association
It can be achieved through differential reinforcement
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Discrimination is the differential recognition of and response to two or more similar stimuli.

questions.question_text: With regard to incubation, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The increase in strength of conditioned response results from repeated brief exposure to the conditioned stimulus
It could explain how phobias are perpetuated
A reduction in the emotional response as a result of escape from a phobic object is a negative reinforcement leading to incubation
It was demonstrated by Watson and Rayner in the Little Albert experiment
The incubation theory of phobic fear was proposed by Eysenck

correct_answer.text: It was demonstrated by Watson and Rayner in the Little Albert experiment

correct_answers.text: It was demonstrated by Watson and Rayner in the Little Albert experiment

questions.explanation: Watson and Rayner demonstrated generalization in the Little Albert experiment.

questions.question_text: In learning theory:

options.text: Stimulus preparedness means that specific objects like blood and snakes are much more likely to be the subject of phobias than others
Temporal contiguity between the conditioned stimulus and unconditioned stimulus is the most important factor in the development of classical conditioning
In classical conditioning, conditioned responses are likely to be of greater magnitude than unconditioned responses
A higher-order conditioning uses a conditioned response as an unconditioned stimulus
The learning occurs only if the subject's behaviour is reinforced

correct_answer.text: Stimulus preparedness means that specific objects like blood and snakes are much more likely to be the subject of phobias than others

correct_answers.text: Stimulus preparedness means that specific objects like blood and snakes are much more likely to be the subject of phobias than others

questions.explanation: A higher predictability, that is a higher probability of unconditioned stimulus occurring with conditioned stimulus, is more important than temporal contiguity. Conditioned responses are lesser in magnitude. A higher-order conditioning uses a conditioned stimulus as an unconditioned stimulus. Vicarious learning occurs without reinforcement.

questions.question_text: Regarding operant conditioning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Thorndike described operant and respondent behaviours
A voluntary behaviour is engaged in because its occurrence is reinforced by being rewarded
A voluntary behaviour independent of stimuli is termed operant behaviour
A behaviour that is dependent on known stimuli is termed respondent behaviour
Thorndike's law of effect holds that voluntary behaviour that is paired with subsequent reward is strengthened

correct_answer.text: Thorndike described operant and respondent behaviours

correct_answers.text: Thorndike described operant and respondent behaviours

questions.explanation: Skinner described operant and respondent behaviours.

questions.question_text: Regarding positive reinforcement, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It is synonymous with reward
It is a pleasant stimulus that follows a desired behaviour
It increases the likelihood of the desired behaviour
Allowing a child to leave his room only when he is no longer having a temper tantrum is an example
A high grade on an examination is an example

correct_answer.text: Allowing a child to leave his room only when he is no longer having a temper tantrum is an example

correct_answers.text: Allowing a child to leave his room only when he is no longer having a temper tantrum is an example

questions.explanation: Allowing a child to leave his room when he is no longer having a temper tantrum is an example of negative reinforcement.

questions.question_text: Removal of an unpleasant stimulus after a desired behaviour occurs is:

options.text: Positive reinforcement
Negative reinforcement
Positive punishment
Negative punishment
Primary reinforcement

correct_answer.text: Negative reinforcement

correct_answers.text: Negative reinforcement

questions.explanation: A negative reinforcer is an aversive stimulus whose removal increases the probability of occurrence of the operant behaviour. Punishment is the situation that occurs if an aversive stimulus is presented whenever the given behaviour occurs, thereby reducing the probability of occurrence of this response.

questions.question_text: Regarding types of reinforcement and punishment, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Negative reinforcement increases the likelihood of the desired behaviour
Negative punishment is removal of a pleasant stimulus after a desired behaviour occurs
Positive punishment is presentation of an unpleasant stimulus after an undesired behaviour occurs
Positive punishment decreases the likelihood of the undesired behaviour
Negative punishment decreases the likelihood of the undesired behaviour

correct_answer.text: Negative punishment is removal of a pleasant stimulus after a desired behaviour occurs

correct_answers.text: Negative punishment is removal of a pleasant stimulus after a desired behaviour occurs

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the removal of a pleasant stimulus after an undesired behaviour occurs.

questions.question_text: Regarding reinforcement, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Primary reinforcers are those stimuli that meet biological needs
Secondary reinforcers are those that one has to learn the value of
Punishment tends not to be so effective in learning situations as positive or negative reinforcers
In continuous reinforcement, reinforcement takes place following every conditioned response
Continuous reinforcement is not good at maintaining a high response rate

correct_answer.text: Continuous reinforcement is not good at maintaining a high response rate

correct_answers.text: Continuous reinforcement is not good at maintaining a high response rate

questions.explanation: Continuous reinforcement leads to the maximum response rate.

questions.question_text: With regard to conditioning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In avoidance conditioning, fear reduction is a positive reinforcement
Avoidance conditioning demonstrates principles of both classical and operant conditioning
Escape conditioning is a variety of negative conditioning
When it is learnt, escape from an aversive stimulus is very resistant to extinction
An extreme punishment may elicit aggressive behaviour that is more serious than the original undesirable behaviour

correct_answer.text: In avoidance conditioning, fear reduction is a positive reinforcement

correct_answers.text: In avoidance conditioning, fear reduction is a positive reinforcement

questions.explanation: In avoidance conditioning, fear reduction is a negative reinforcement.

questions.question_text: In partial reinforcement, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Fixed interval schedule is poor in maintaining the conditioned response
Variable interval schedule is very good in maintaining the conditioned response
Fixed ratio schedule is very poor in maintaining a high response rate
Variable ratio schedule is very good in maintaining a high response rate
Variable ratio schedule is more likely to produce emotional outbursts during the learning phase

correct_answer.text: Fixed ratio schedule is very poor in maintaining a high response rate

correct_answers.text: Fixed ratio schedule is very poor in maintaining a high response rate

questions.explanation: In partial reinforcement, only some of the conditioned responses are reinforced. Fixed ratio schedule is good in maintaining a high response rate.

questions.question_text: Behavioural explanation of the aetiology of phobias includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Habituation
Stimulus preparedness
Incubation
Escape conditioning
Avoidance conditioning

correct_answer.text: Habituation

correct_answers.text: Habituation

questions.explanation: Habituation is an important principle of behavioural treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: Reciprocal inhibition:

options.text: Is based on Wolpe's principle
Is used to treat conditions associated with anticipatory anxiety
Is based on the concept that desired and undesired behaviours are incompatible, which facilitates changes in the desired direction
Is used in systematic desensitization
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The theory of reciprocal inhibition is used to treat phobias through counter-conditioning.

questions.question_text: Habituation is:

options.text: An example of counter-conditioning
Applied in systematic desensitization
Applied in exposure and response prevention
The process by which an organism learns to weaken its reaction to a weak stimulus that has no serious consequences
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Habituation is used in treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following are paired correctly, except:

options.text: Flooding–Enforced exposure
Modelling–Vicarious exposure
Chaining–Complex behaviour learned in separate steps
Shaping–Explains behavioural disturbances in learning disability
Cueing–Based on operant conditioning

correct_answer.text: Shaping–Explains behavioural disturbances in learning disability

correct_answers.text: Shaping–Explains behavioural disturbances in learning disability

questions.explanation: Shaping is used to manage behavioural disturbances in learning disability.

questions.question_text: All of the following are components of Bandura's observational learning model, except:

options.text: Attention
Perception
Generalization
Memory
Motivation

correct_answer.text: Generalization

correct_answers.text: Generalization

questions.explanation: Generalization is a component of associative learning.

questions.question_text: In observational learning:

options.text: Symbolic modelling is more effective than live modelling
The concept of reciprocal determinism is important
Modelling cannot be used in a group setting
Principles of classical and operant conditioning are excluded
All of the above

correct_answer.text: The concept of reciprocal determinism is important

correct_answers.text: The concept of reciprocal determinism is important

questions.explanation: Live modelling is more effective than symbolic modelling. Modelling is used in group settings in psychotherapy; it includes principles of both classical and operant conditioning.

questions.question_text: With regard to cognitive learning, which of the following statements are true?

options.text: The cognitive map is associated with T olman's model
The concept of insight learning is associated with Kohler
Complex learning occurs in two phases
Complex learning is intimately related to memory and thinking
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Complex learning occurs in two phases: insight learning and latent learning.

questions.question_text: In psychoanalytic models of learning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Behaviour is determined by intrapsychic processes
Problem behaviour is the focus of the study and the treatment
Childhood experiences are the focus of analysis
Problem behaviour is a symptom of unconscious conflict
Subjective methods of interpretation of behaviour are used

correct_answer.text: Problem behaviour is the focus of the study and the treatment

correct_answers.text: Problem behaviour is the focus of the study and the treatment

questions.explanation: In the behavioural model, problem behaviour is the focus of the study and the treatment, and in the psychoanalytic model the underlying unconscious conflict is the focus of the treatment.

questions.question_text: In the behavioural model of learning, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Behaviour is determined by current contingencies
Behaviour is determined by reinforcement history
Behaviour is determined by genetic endowment
Behaviour is determined by intrapsychic processes
Behaviour is determined by needs deriving from basic drives

correct_answer.text: Behaviour is determined by intrapsychic processes

correct_answers.text: Behaviour is determined by intrapsychic processes

questions.explanation: Intrapsychic processes are part of psychoanalytic models.

questions.question_text: Functional analysis in behavioural therapy includes all of the following, except:

options.text: A direct record of the frequency of occurrence of the behaviour studied
A direct record of the duration of occurrence of the behaviour studied
A direct record of the intensity of the behaviour studied
A direct record of the defence mechanisms in the behaviour studied
A direct record of the stimuli increasing the incidence of the behaviour studied

correct_answer.text: A direct record of the defence mechanisms in the behaviour studied

correct_answers.text: A direct record of the defence mechanisms in the behaviour studied

questions.explanation: Functional analysis in behavioural therapy does not include recording of defence mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Optimal conditions for observational learning include:

options.text: The behaviour observed is being reinforced
Perceived similarity
Active participation
Familiarity of the model
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Observational learning can occur without direct reinforcement.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about modelling, except:

options.text: It can improve self-efficacy
It can decrease aggression
It can eliminate negative behaviour patterns and decrease anxiety threshold
It can be used in weight-reduction programmes
It cannot lower the pain threshold

correct_answer.text: It cannot lower the pain threshold

correct_answers.text: It cannot lower the pain threshold

questions.explanation: Modelling can lower the pain threshold.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true, except:

options.text: Observational learning can occur without reinforcement
When a person dislikes a model, imitative behaviour is less likely to occur
Insight learning does not require understanding of the relationship between various elements of the problem to be solved
Latent learning is manifested when there is a need to satisfy a basic drive
According to tension reduction theory, people are completely unaware of their avoidance patterns

correct_answer.text: Insight learning does not require understanding of the relationship between various elements of the problem to be solved

correct_answers.text: Insight learning does not require understanding of the relationship between various elements of the problem to be solved

questions.explanation: Insight learning is based on prior understanding.

questions.question_text: All of the following names are correctly paired with their associated theories, except:

options.text: Wolpe–Anxiety hierarchy
Dollard and Miller–T ension reduction theory
Beck–Learned helplessness model of depression
Kandel–Habituation and sensitization
Harlow–Learning set

correct_answer.text: Beck–Learned helplessness model of depression

correct_answers.text: Beck–Learned helplessness model of depression

questions.explanation: Beck is associated with the cognitive triad and Seligman with the learned helplessness model of depression.

questions.question_text: Regarding imprinting, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: It is an ethological concept
It was described by Lorenz
It is an important component of behavioural treatment of phobias
It is normally species specific
All of the above

correct_answer.text: It is an important component of behavioural treatment of phobias

correct_answers.text: It is an important component of behavioural treatment of phobias

questions.explanation: An example of imprinting is that a goose follows the first moving object it sees after it hatches.

questions.question_text: Regarding application of learning theory in behavioural psychology, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Only a quarter of animal phobias are associated with prior traumatic experience with animals
We may be prepared to acquire certain fears on evolutionary grounds
Exposure therapy for anxiety disorders depends on habituation
Self-exposure should be attempted only with intense supervision from the therapist
More effective exposure occurs in real life than in the imagination

correct_answer.text: Self-exposure should be attempted only with intense supervision from the therapist

correct_answers.text: Self-exposure should be attempted only with intense supervision from the therapist

questions.explanation: Only 23% of animal phobias are associated with prior traumatic experience with animals (McNally & Steketee 1985); many patients can carry out self-exposure effectively with intervention only from the therapist; more effective exposure occurs in real life than in the imagination (Emmelkamp & Wessels 1975).

questions.question_text: With regard to behavioural therapy, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: For specific phobias, 70–80% of patients are successfully treated
For agoraphobia, exposure has been shown to be more effective than waiting and attention controls, and as effective as medication
The combination of exposure and high-dose benzodiazepines is more effective for agoraphobia than exposure alone
In the short term, antidepressants plus exposure are the most effective treatment for panic and agoraphobia
Meta-analytic studies have shown exposure to be a more effective treatment for social phobia

correct_answer.text: The combination of exposure and high-dose benzodiazepines is more effective for agoraphobia than exposure alone

correct_answers.text: The combination of exposure and high-dose benzodiazepines is more effective for agoraphobia than exposure alone

questions.explanation: Exposure has been shown to be more effective than waiting and attention controls (DeRubeis & Crits-Cristoph 1998); the combination of exposure and high-dose benzodiazepines is less effective for agoraphobia than exposure alone (Marks et al 1993); antidepressants plus exposure are the most effective treatment (van Balkom et al 1997); meta-analytic studies have shown exposure to be a more effective treatment for social phobia (Chambless and Gillis 1993).

questions.question_text: Functional behaviour assessment includes:

options.text: Exploration of the childhood origins of antecedents
Family history and dynamics
Expressed emotions in the family
An understanding of incubation
Assessment of the patient's projection

correct_answer.text: An understanding of incubation

correct_answers.text: An understanding of incubation

questions.explanation: Functional behaviour assessment includes an account of the antecedents, the behaviour and the consequences; incubation is the increase in strength of conditioned response resulting from repeated brief exposure to the conditioned stimuli, and hence is important in ABC analysis.

questions.question_text: The following clinical applications of behaviour therapy are all correctly paired, except:

options.text: Agoraphobia–Graded exposure and flooding
Alcohol dependence–Exposure and response prevention
Schizophrenia–The token economy procedure
Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)–Eye movement desensitiza-tion and reprocessing (EMDR)
Type A behaviour–Biofeedback

correct_answer.text: Alcohol dependence–Exposure and response prevention

correct_answers.text: Alcohol dependence–Exposure and response prevention

questions.explanation: In alcohol dependency, aversion therapy is used; exposure and response prevention are mainly used to treat obsessive compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: With regard to aversion therapy, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: A noxious stimulus is presented immediately after a specific behavioural response
Covert sensitization is a form of behaviour therapy in which an undesirable behaviour is paired with an unpleasant image in order to eliminate that behaviour
Aversion therapy can be used to treat behaviours with impulsive qualities
Punishment always leads to the expected decrease in response
Punishment can sometimes be positively reinforcing

correct_answer.text: Punishment always leads to the expected decrease in response

correct_answers.text: Punishment always leads to the expected decrease in response

questions.explanation: Punishment can effectively eliminate an undesirable response if it is consistent and is delivered immediately after the undesired response, and if an alternative response is rewarded. But when punishment fails to give an alternative response, the organism may substitute a less desirable response for the punished one.

questions.question_text: With regard to application of learning principles to treatment, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In systematic desensitization, the learned relaxation state and the anxiety-provoking scenes are systematically paired in the treatment
In systematic desensitization, a conditioned stimulus is used to avoid an unconditioned painful stimulus
Stimulus preparedness of some phobias may make them more difficult to treat
Response prevention is characteristically combined with flooding
Implosion is flooding achieved in the imagination rather than in real life

correct_answer.text: In systematic desensitization, a conditioned stimulus is used to avoid an unconditioned painful stimulus

correct_answers.text: In systematic desensitization, a conditioned stimulus is used to avoid an unconditioned painful stimulus

questions.explanation: In systematic desensitization, patients attain a state of complete relaxation and are then exposed to the stimulus that elicits the anxiety response. The negative reaction of anxiety is inhibited by the relaxed state, a process called reciprocal inhibition.

questions.question_text: In learning and conditioning:

options.text: Operant conditioning is contingent on a particular stimulus
Punishment contingent upon response leads to learned helplessness
In operant conditioning, the behaviour preceding the reinforcer always alters in frequency
Counter-conditioning and reciprocal inhibition are involved in systematic desensitization
Habituation explains generalization

correct_answer.text: Counter-conditioning and reciprocal inhibition are involved in systematic desensitization

correct_answers.text: Counter-conditioning and reciprocal inhibition are involved in systematic desensitization

questions.explanation: Operant conditioning occurs only when the organism feels a contingency between its response and reinforcement, and hence is contingent on an anticipatory response.

questions.question_text: All of the following are related to aetiology and maintenance of phobias, except:

options.text: Avoidance learning
Seligman's preparedness theory
Stimulus generalization
Magnification and minimization
Fear of castration

correct_answer.text: Magnification and minimization

correct_answers.text: Magnification and minimization

questions.explanation: Magnification and minimization are cognitive distortions in depression.

questions.question_text: All of the following are involved in the aetiology and maintenance of agoraphobia, except:

options.text: Avoidance conditioning
Escape conditioning
Sensitization
Over-inclusion
Incubation

correct_answer.text: Over-inclusion

correct_answers.text: Over-inclusion

questions.explanation: Over-inclusion (over-inclusive thinking) is a type of thinking described in schizophrenia where the patient is unable to preserve conceptual boundaries.

questions.question_text: With regard to application of learning principles:

options.text: Vicarious learning involves extinction
In a behavioural assessment it is important to understand the patient's projections
Classical conditioning explains how anxiety arises in response to environmental stimuli
Learned helplessness is an example of classical conditioning
In operant conditioning, the reinforcer precedes the behaviour

correct_answer.text: Classical conditioning explains how anxiety arises in response to environmental stimuli

correct_answers.text: Classical conditioning explains how anxiety arises in response to environmental stimuli

questions.explanation: Forgetting is different from extinction; in operant conditioning, a reinforcer is anything that increases the probability of a response when it follows the response.

questions.question_text: Regarding Eysenck's contribution to personality theories, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: The personality dimensions extroversion, neuroticism and psychoti-cism are normally distributed
Extroversion exists as a balance between excitation and inhibition processes in the ascending reticular activating system
Neuroticism is connected to the reactivity of the autonomic nervous system
Eysenck's Personality Inventory is a self-reported questionnaire to assess the three personality dimensions
Eysenck's Personality Inventory contains an index assessing response bias

correct_answer.text: The personality dimensions extroversion, neuroticism and psychoti-cism are normally distributed

correct_answers.text: The personality dimensions extroversion, neuroticism and psychoti-cism are normally distributed

questions.explanation: The personality dimensions extroversion and neuroticism are normally distributed, whereas psychoticism is not.

questions.question_text: Regarding personality theories, all of the following are correct, except:

options.text: Cattell used factor analytic studies
Allport described common traits and individual traits
Kelly's personal construct theory proposes that the construct system is hierarchically organized
Bannister devised the Construct Repertory T est
Q-sort technique is devised from a theory based on Rogers's client-centred therapy

correct_answer.text: Bannister devised the Construct Repertory T est

correct_answers.text: Bannister devised the Construct Repertory T est

questions.explanation: Kelly devised the Construct Repertory T est for eliciting a person's personal constructs.

questions.question_text: Regarding the psychoanalytic approach to personality structure, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In Freud's structural model of the mind, all of the id is submerged in the unconscious
In Freud's structural model of the mind, most of the ego is submerged in the unconscious
In Freud's structural model of the mind, most of the superego is in the conscious or in the preconscious
A child resolves the oedipal conflict by identifying with the same-sex parent

Recent psychodynamic theorists believe that ego performs other functions besides finding ways to satisfy id impulses, including learning how to cope with the environment and making sense of experience

correct_answer.text: In Freud's structural model of the mind, most of the superego is in the conscious or in the preconscious

correct_answers.text: In Freud's structural model of the mind, most of the superego is in the conscious or in the preconscious

questions.explanation: In Freud's structural model of the mind, small parts of the ego and superego are either in the conscious or in the preconscious.

questions.question_text: Carl Rogers:

options.text: Introduced non-directive psychotherapy
Believed that individuals have an innate tendency to move toward growth, maturity and positive change, described as actualizing tendency
Argued that people are likely to function more effectively if they feel they are valued by their parents regardless of their feelings, attitudes and behaviours
Described the form of psychotherapy in which the therapist's role is to act as a sounding board while the client explores and analyses his or her own problems
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Non-directive psychotherapy is the same as client-centred therapy.

questions.question_text: Regarding cognitive approaches of personality theories, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: According to Kelly, personal constructs take an either/or form
Differences in self-schemas produce differences in behaviour
A person whose self-schema includes being physically fit is less likely to exercise regularly
According to Bem's gender-schema theory, individuals who describe themselves as having both masculine and feminine traits are referred to as androgynous
None of the above

correct_answer.text: A person whose self-schema includes being physically fit is less likely to exercise regularly

correct_answers.text: A person whose self-schema includes being physically fit is less likely to exercise regularly

questions.explanation: A person whose self-schema includes being physically fit is more likely to exercise regularly.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about sleep stages, except:

options.text: Most REM sleep occurs in the last part of the night
Sleepers who are awakened during REM sleep report a dream about 50% of the time
During NREM sleep, heart and breathing rates decrease markedly
During REM sleep, the body is almost paralysed, except the muscles of the vital organs
In REM sleep, the metabolic rate of the brain increases somewhat compared with during wakefulness

correct_answer.text: Sleepers who are awakened during REM sleep report a dream about 50% of the time

correct_answers.text: Sleepers who are awakened during REM sleep report a dream about 50% of the time

questions.explanation: Sleepers who are awakened during NREM sleep report a dream about 50% of the time; sleepers who are awakened during REM sleep almost always report a dream.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about the pattern of variation of sleep cycle with age, except:

options.text: Newborn infants spend half their sleeping time in REM sleep
The proportion of REM sleep drops to 20–25% of total sleep time by age 5 and remains fairly constant until old age
Older people tend to experience more stage 3 and 4 sleep
REM sleep drops to 18% or less at old age
A natural kind of insomnia sets in as people grow older

correct_answer.text: Older people tend to experience more stage 3 and 4 sleep

correct_answers.text: Older people tend to experience more stage 3 and 4 sleep

questions.explanation: Older people tend to experience less stage 3 and 4 sleep.

questions.question_text: In the sleep–wake cycle:

options.text: In REM sleep, the brain is largely isolated from its sensory and motor channels
The dreams reported when a person is roused from REM sleep tend to be visually vivid, with emotional and illogical features.
The longer the period of REM sleep before arousal, the longer and more elaborate is the reported dream.
NREM dreams are more directly related to what is happening in the person's waking life.
All of the above are true

correct_answer.text: All of the above are true

correct_answers.text: All of the above are true

questions.explanation: NREM sleep is associated with serotoninergic neuronal activity in the raphe complex; REM sleep is associated with noradrenergic neuronal activity.

questions.question_text: Regarding states of consciousness, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Narcolepsy is regarded as the intrusion of REM episodes into daytime hours
Some people are more readily hypnotized than others, although most people show some susceptibility
Reduction of pain is one of the beneficial uses of hypnosis
Sleep spindles and K complexes occur in stage 4 sleep
Penile erection is common in REM sleep

correct_answer.text: Sleep spindles and K complexes occur in stage 4 sleep

correct_answers.text: Sleep spindles and K complexes occur in stage 4 sleep

questions.explanation: Sleep spindles and K complexes occur in stage 2 sleep.
